2017_111_081517mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of August 15, 2017 at the Administration Building — a short back-to-school meeting with no recognition items. It opens 90 ninth-grade Schools of Choice seats at International Academy East for 2018-2019 and awards $44,682.00 to Tyco SimplexGrinnell for a video surveillance software upgrade forced by the City of Troy's move to Pelco VideoXpert. The July 18 minutes carried here record the decision that would define the fall: the Board placed a 1-mill building and site sinking fund on a November 7, 2017 special election ballot, 6-1 with Mrs. Hammond opposed.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, August 15, 2017, 7:00 PM, **Administration Building**, 4400 Livernois — not the usual Services Building. No recognition items.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the July 18 special workshop and July 18 meeting, and the June 2017 Treasurer's Report.

**What the July 18 minutes record**
The special workshop (6:15–7:40 p.m.) covered a teaching and learning report and a business update on the **Building and Site Sinking Fund Tax Proposal**. The regular meeting followed at 7:46.

Administrator contracts were extended — the roster names Ryan Brinks at IA-East, Lara Dixon at Athens, Remo Roncone at Troy High, Joe Duda at Larson, **Timothy Fulcher at Smith**, **Audra Melton at Baker**, Joyce Brasington, **Janice Brzezinski at Hill**, Brian Canfield, Mike Cottone, Tammy DiPonio, Sarah Glasser, Matt Jansen, Melanie Morey, **John Pagel at Martell**, Jeremey Whan, and assistant principals Melissa Curth, Robert Dowd, Dan House, Dan Mills, William Turner, Brian Zawislak, Amy Buchanan, **Jonathan Cross at Baker** and **Anthony Morse at Boulan Park**. Nearly all of these names recur in the May 2018 reshuffle: Fulcher to athletics, Pagel to employee services, Cross and Morse to principalships, Brzezinski and Melton to the retiree list.

Added to the agenda that night was a Leonard principal appointment: **Dr. Erin Detmer**, approved 7-0 — the Hill literacy specialist whose Teachers College coaching work the Board had recognized in May.

**Resolution 17-072 — the sinking fund goes to the ballot.** The recitals state that the district is a Michigan general powers school district whose elections are governed by the Michigan Election Law, Public Act 116 of 1954; that **in order to improve and repair its facilities it is necessary to ask the voters to approve a building and site sinking fund tax levy of one (1) mill annually for a period of ten (10) years from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028**; and that the district wishes to submit the proposal at a **Special School Election on November 7, 2017**. Ballot language must be certified to the Election Coordinator by 4:00 p.m. on **August 15, 2017** — the day of this very meeting.

The vote was **6 yes, 1 no — Mrs. Hammond**. This is the proposal the Epic MRA survey had tested in April, which found 61% outright Yes at one mill and warned repeatedly that raising the ask would collapse support; the Board asked for exactly one mill.

**Treasurer's Report — June 2017**
The fiscal year's closing month. Total check disbursements are **$12,522,371.11**, the General Fund group $9,310,856.14 and the General Fund (101) itself $8,670,831.46. Adding $3,352,991.59 of wire transfers, $165,585.20 of P-Card purchases and $24,980.62 of ACH debits, less $671.00 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are **$16,065,257.52**.

**Curriculum — 90 seats at IA East**
The Board adopts a Section 105c resolution accepting applications for **90 non-resident 9th grade students** who reside outside Oakland County, where that ISD is contiguous with Oakland ISD's boundaries, for the purpose of attending the International Academy East program. Like the August 2018 version, this is a 105c-only resolution adopted more than a year ahead of the school year it governs; the seat count would drop to 85 the following August.

**Business — the surveillance upgrade**
The district shares its video surveillance system with the City of Troy, and the City is moving to Pelco's latest **VideoXpert** platform. Beth Soggs' July 26 memo — her first business item as the Director of Technology appointed in May — explains that the current Pelco software used by both is **discontinued, with an end-of-support announcement expected**, and that the City wants to stay on a supported platform.

At the time of the City's upgrade the district's system converts to a **standalone Pelco VideoXpert Enterprise system**, with the City repurposing some of its existing hardware to supply what the district needs. Afterward the district manages its own system, the City retaining view access to district cameras. The practical gain is access: today footage can be reached only from a few specific computers and is slow because of the connection speed between City and District; the new configuration lets the Pelco client run on any computer on the district network, giving Safe-Ed and building administration far better access and search.

The award is **Tyco SimplexGrinnell, $44,682.00**, from the General Fund.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, August 15, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition (none); 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the July 18, 2017 Special Board of Education Workshop, B. Minutes of the July 18, 2017 Board of Education Meeting, C. Treasurer's Report – June 2017; 6. Personnel — A. Consideration: Elementary and Secondary; 7. Curriculum — A. Consideration: IA-East Schools of Choice, Section 105C for 9th Grade for 2018/2019 School Year; 8. Business — A. Consideration: Video Surveillance Software System Update; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Consent minutes: the July 18, 2017 special board workshop.** President Philippart called the workshop to order at 6:15 p.m. with all seven members present — Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Schmidt — along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West, and three members of the audience. The agenda was public communication; a teaching and learning update covering the Teaching & Learning and Secondary Report; and a business update on the Building and Site Sinking Fund Tax Proposal. It adjourned at 7:40 p.m., six minutes before the regular meeting began.

**Consent minutes: the July 18, 2017 regular meeting.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:46 p.m. with all seven members present, Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West, and approximately seven members of the audience. There were no recognitions and no public communication. Dr. Machesky informed President Philippart that there was an addition to the agenda: item 6.D, an administrative appointment for the Leonard principal, would be presented for consideration.

Resolution 17-066 approved the consent agenda: minutes of the June 6, 2017 special meeting and closed session; the June 6, 2017 meeting; the June 13, 2017 special meeting and closed session; the June 13, 2017 workshop; the June 20, 2017 special meeting and closed session; and the June 20, 2017 meeting.

Resolutions 17-067 through 17-069 covered the administrative contract extensions. The roster of administrators names Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal, International Academy-East; Lara Dixon, Principal, Athens High School; Remo Roncone, Principal, Troy High School; Joe Duda, Principal, Larson Middle School; Timothy Fulcher, Principal, Smith Middle School; Audra Melton, Principal, Baker Middle School; Joyce Brasington, Principal, Wattles Elementary School; Janice Brzezinski, Principal, Hill Elementary School; Brian Canfield, Principal, Schroeder Elementary School; Mike Cottone, Principal, Troy Union Elementary School; Tammy DiPonio, Principal, Costello Elementary School; Sarah Glasser, Principal, Hamilton Elementary School; Matt Jansen, Principal, Wass Elementary School; Melanie Morey, Principal, Barnard Elementary School; John Pagel, Principal, Martell Elementary School; Jeremey Whan, Principal, Bemis Elementary School; Melissa Curth, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Robert Dowd, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Dan House, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Dan Mills, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; William Turner, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Brian Zawislak, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Amy Buchanan, Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School; Jonathan Cross, Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School; and Anthony Morse, Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School.

Read against the May 2018 packet, this roster is a snapshot taken ten months before a substantial reshuffle: Timothy Fulcher would move from the Smith principalship to Director of Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment; John Pagel from Martell to Director, Employee Services; Jonathan Cross from assistant principal at Baker to its principalship; Anthony Morse from assistant principal at Boulan Park to its principalship; and Janice Brzezinski and Audra Melton would both appear on the 2018 retiree list.

A further resolution approved Dr. Erin Detmer's employment as Principal, Leonard Elementary School, 7-0 — the item added to the agenda that evening. Detmer is the Hill literacy specialist whose work with the Teachers College coaching model the Board had recognized two months earlier, moving from literacy specialist to building principal.

Resolution 17-071 addressed the six secondary schools for 2016/2017.

**Resolution 17-072: the Building and Site Sinking Fund Tax Proposal for a Special School Election on November 7, 2017.** Moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mr. Hauff, the resolution recites that the School District is a Michigan general powers school district operating under the Revised School Code, and as such its elections are governed by the Michigan Election Law, Public Act 116 of 1954, as amended; that the School District has determined that in order to improve and repair its facilities it is necessary to ask the voters to approve a building and site sinking fund tax levy of one mill annually for a period of ten years from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028; that the district desires to submit the proposal to the voters at a Special School Election to be held on November 7, 2017; that the Michigan Election Law requires the district to certify ballot language for any proposals to the district's Election Coordinator not later than 4:00 p.m. local time on the twelfth Tuesday before the election date; and that the district desires to approve the proposal and authorize the Superintendent or his designee to certify the ballot language.

It resolves that the Building and Site Sinking Fund Tax Proposal attached as Exhibit A is approved; that the Superintendent or his designee is authorized to certify the Proposal to the district's Election Coordinator not later than 4:00 p.m. local time on August 15, 2017; and further authorizes the Superintendent or designee to take related steps.

The vote was 6 yes, 1 no — Mrs. Hammond. It is the only recorded dissent in the July meeting and one of the few in these 2017 packets, where nearly every resolution carries unanimously.

Two details are worth drawing out. First, the certification deadline in the resolution is 4:00 p.m. on August 15, 2017 — the date of the very meeting whose packet carries these minutes, meaning the ballot language had to be filed the same day the Board next convened. Second, the ask is exactly one mill. The Epic MRA community survey delivered to the Board on June 13 had tested precisely that figure, found 61% outright Yes with 7% leaning yes, and stated in identical words across three separate slides that tax neutrality is what earns the community's endorsement and that raising the ask collapses support. The survey background had also noted the countervailing pressure — that a district can pursue only one sinking fund every ten years, so there is reason to ask for more. The Board asked for one mill, over a single dissent.

**Treasurer's Report, June 2017.** General Fund (101) check disbursements are $8,670,831.46, with Total General Fund of $9,310,856.14 and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS of $12,522,371.11. Adding ACH debits of $24,980.62, outgoing wire transfers of $3,352,991.59 and P-Card purchases of $165,585.20, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $671.00, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $16,065,257.52 — the largest month of the fiscal year, as June closes out contracts, capital work and the year's payroll obligations. The middle sections of the packet are the June check register run by fund.

**Personnel 6.A: elementary and secondary.** The item covers the personnel recommendations for the incoming school year.

**Curriculum 7.A: Schools of Choice, Section 105c, 9th grade for 2018-2019.** In accordance with Michigan state law, school districts shall pass a resolution each school year if they intend to participate in a Schools of Choice program. It is anticipated that seats will be available for the 2018-2019 school year for grade 9 at the International Academy East, and the item proposes a Section 105c resolution for 90 non-resident 9th grade students who reside outside of Oakland County, if that intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries.

The resolution provides that the Board of Education of the Troy School District, exercising the option permitted by Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, will accept applications for a Schools of Choice program for the 2018-2019 school year for 90 non-resident 9th grade students who reside outside Oakland County, if that Intermediate School District is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the purposes of attending the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District.

As with the equivalent resolution adopted in August 2018, this is a 105c-only measure — the International Academy is a consortium program drawing from beyond the county by design, so there is no companion Section 105 resolution as there is for the district's elementary and middle school seats. It is also adopted more than a year ahead of the school year it governs. The seat count would be reduced from 90 to 85 in the following year's resolution.

**Business 8.A: video surveillance software system upgrade.** The Troy School District collaborates with the City of Troy for its video surveillance system. The City needs to update its system, which also requires the district to update its software.

Beth Soggs' July 26, 2017 memorandum to the Board explains the situation — her first business item in the packets as the Director of Technology appointed in May. The City needs to update its system to Pelco's latest VideoXpert software platform, and as a result the district also needs to update its software. The current Pelco software utilized by both the City and the district has been discontinued by Pelco, and an end of support announcement is expected in the future; the City wants to ensure it remains on a supported platform and desires several of the features available in the new software.

At the time of the City upgrade, the district's system will be converted to a standalone Pelco VideoXpert Enterprise system. The City will repurpose some of its existing hardware to provide the district the hardware necessary for this configuration and software update. After the update, the district will manage its own system on the updated platform, with the City retaining access to view district cameras.

Soggs sets out the benefits, which are about access rather than image quality. With the current configuration, footage can only be accessed from a few specific computers in the district, and access is slow due to the connection speed between City and district. The updated software and configuration allows the Pelco client to be installed on computers anywhere on the district network, providing greater access to Safe-Ed and building administration, and better search capabilities.

The resolution awards the video surveillance software upgrade to Tyco SimplexGrinnell in the amount of $44,682.00 as an expenditure of the General Fund. The packet attaches system documentation for both the City of Troy Police Department and the Troy School District video surveillance systems.

The arrangement is a small but revealing piece of municipal infrastructure: the school district's camera system is not its own but a shared platform with the city police department, and a vendor's end-of-life announcement on the City side obliges the district to spend $44,682.00 and take on management of a standalone system it had not previously run. The upgrade's chief benefit — that Safe-Ed and building administrators can reach footage from any district computer rather than a handful — connects directly to the Safe-Ed security contract the Board had renewed for three years the month before.

Read as a whole, the August 2017 packet is thin on its own business and heavy in what it carries forward. Its two actions are 90 out-of-county seats at IA East and a $44,682.00 software upgrade the City's vendor forced. But the July minutes reproduced in it record the year's pivotal decision — a one-mill, ten-year building and site sinking fund placed on the November 7 ballot, certified the same day this meeting convened, adopted 6-1 at exactly the figure the district's own polling said the community would support and no more.
